Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 4.6 with bigger context window

By Simon Willison · April 18 2026

Anthropic today announced Claude Sonnet 4.6, a new flagship model that extends the context window to 1,000,000 tokens while keeping the same per-token pricing as the previous generation. The update ships alongside a revamped Claude Code CLI, a long-running background agent mode, and a set of developer-facing tools that let you pipe skill files directly into the system prompt.

The context window bump is the headline number, but the more interesting change is the new batching API which reduces the observed latency for multi-turn agent workflows. Anthropic claims a 40% reduction in wall-clock time for a 50-turn coding session.

Benchmarks released with the launch show Sonnet 4.6 matching or beating GPT-5 on SWE-bench Verified, GAIA and MMLU, while coming in at roughly half the output token cost of Claude Opus 4.6. For agent builders this is a meaningful re-pricing of the mid-tier model slot.

Jensen Huang, interviewed on CNBC Television earlier this week, said NVIDIA's latest Blackwell clusters were explicitly sized to serve long-context models of this class. He put the unit economics at "roughly 40 percent better tokens-per-watt than Hopper" for prompts over 200k tokens.

Anthropic is pairing the release with a new developer tier that bundles 1M tokens of free evaluation credit for teams building on the Claude Agent SDK. The company expects most shipping agents will move to Sonnet 4.6 within 90 days.
